corrections.before:
The conditional local heat-component price is approximately $361.2 million per 10 MSA QALYs, not complete portfolio cost-effectiveness.

The denominator is three years of the entire charitable recipient's gross operating expense. The scenario assumes an additional cooling-implementation package could reduce the city's annual heat mortality envelope by 1% beyond already funded and mandated protections. A 25% coalition probability, 20% WE ACT contribution and 50% ordinary funding response yield 0.125 attributable deaths avoided annually for five cohorts starting four years from valuation. These are transparent priors, not measured effects. Each death avoided is valued at no more than five remaining years with 0.6 utility and a 20% annual competing-mortality hazard, discounted 3%.

All modeled deaths are NYC-resident deaths, so the component's MSA share is 100%; this does not assign national benefits to New York. The parallel NYC-EJA scenario shares the same coalition opportunity and is correlated, not another independent citywide reduction. A combined giving model would need to reassess joint additionality rather than add both prices or benefits mechanically.

Positive alternatives vary implementation, attribution, funding and survival. Complete replacement and a one-QALY adverse outcome are retained. Added $1 million induced household/public cost and 25% coalition-resource cases test omitted costs; neither is a measured invoice. Rent, electricity costs, grid effects and displacement can offset health gains.
